component.name: Wayfinder
component.summary: Fast, native Linux file manager with a docked preview pane

description.p: Wayfinder is a keyboard-friendly Linux file manager built with a permanent side-by-side preview pane so you never lose context while browsing. Click an image to preview it inline, click an audio file to play it right in the panel, or click a text file to read the first few kilobytes — all without opening a separate app.
Features:

ul.li: Docked preview pane with inline image, audio, and text preview
Details and Icons view with adjustable zoom
Click-and-drag rubber-band multi-select for batch operations
Cut, copy, paste, rename, and permanent delete
Tabbed browsing — open multiple directories at once
Folder tree in the sidebar with collapsible sections
Dark theme with a compact, information-dense layout

screenshot.caption: Browse files with a docked preview pane

description.p: Release-audit fixes: no crash when the session bus closes, a finished copy, move or rename always reports itself even when Undo cannot be recorded, the installer never overwrites settings it did not write, and transfer reports have a size limit.

Release-audit fixes: Overwrite and Trash settings warn before anything is deleted for good, outside archive tools only run when their writes can be locked to the destination, and each update redirect is checked before it is followed.
Release-audit fixes: a stuck network drive no longer freezes the window, folder Overwrite warns that it replaces the folder, Move undo never overwrites, and the update download cannot be redirected.
Saving or opening from another app no longer freezes when a slow network drive, such as a Google Drive folder, stops answering.
Sound starts the way it was left instead of always muted, and an unmute is always heard. The preview pane shows Windows shortcuts, Outlook messages and Windows metafile pictures.
Wayfinder starts muted every time, folders can be added under the Network heading, and video thumbnails no longer open the sound output.
The Ask for an update buttons can be clicked in a narrow preview pane, and the duplicate scan no longer walks into another drive mounted inside a scanned folder.

When the preview pane cannot show a file type, it can offer to ask for an update that adds it. Off unless a requests file is set in the config. Unplugging a drive no longer leaves its files listed: the window moves to a folder that still exists and says why.

New "Show original" item in the file menu opens the original of a duplicate in a new window. A video cut out of the middle of an MPEG stream now says it cannot be played instead of leaving the preview blank. Mute and volume are now one setting for every video and song, so a mute no longer silently carries into the next file.
Right-click menus also open from the keyboard (Menu key or Shift+F10). Secondary text is lighter and easier to read. Icon-only buttons have names a screen reader can speak.

AVI files play in the preview, including old Windows codecs. Video files show a picture in List, Details and Compact views. More picture kinds open in the preview (HEIC grids, cut-off PNGs, compressed BMPs), and broken files say why. Startup no longer waits on slow drives. Clicking near the scrollbar no longer throws the list. Clearing a search brings the folder back. Paste errors are in plain words. Compressing files with unusual names is safe.

The PS2 hard drive shows in the sidebar and opens. Plugged-in drives get Unmount and Eject, which wait for a running transfer and never power off a drive that did not fully unmount. Scrolling, rename and preview fixes.
The sidebar no longer freezes the window. Reading the folders behind a drive row now happens on a worker, so a slow or rate-limited network mount can no longer stop the whole window while it answers.
An update check is no longer answered from a stale cached copy, so a new version is seen the moment it is published.
The sidebar icons are the right drawings again, and crisp at every size.
Sidebar rows are their proper height again instead of stretching to fill the space above the drives.

Wayfinder can now tell you when a new version is out and install it for you. It asks the site once a day, and the update is checked against its checksum before anything is unpacked. There is also a Check for Updates item in the options menu.

Deleting an item on a mounted drive reported a failure although the item had moved, because Trash is per filesystem and only the home Trash was being read. The Trash on the item's own volume is used now, and Undo follows it.

Selecting a folder now lists its contents in the preview pane, each row clickable. Icons view lays out as a real grid again, with picture-sized tiles that zoom with Ctrl+scroll. A new sidebar icon set. Every picture previews or says why it cannot, and a refusal is written to a log. A pasted address resolves to its folder. Search skips mounts it cannot finish walking and says when it truncated. The selection survives a change of view, and wayfinder --select opens a folder with one file highlighted.

First public release. The source is now GPL-3.0-or-later. Wayfinder can act as the system file dialog through a desktop portal backend, installs on any desktop with packaging/install.sh, and writes a crash report instead of vanishing. Also: the file dialog, tabbed browsing, a docked preview pane, drives and network shares, trash with undo, and archive browsing.
Initial release. Core file management, preview pane, tabbed browsing, audio playback, and rubber-band multi-select.
